newsitem.title: POLAND: River level drops at threatened Polish border town.
newsitem.headline: River level drops at threatened Polish border town.

text.p: The swollen Oder River has begun receding at the Polish town of Slubice on the German border, suggesting an end may be in sight to a month-long flood crisis, a Polish official said on Sunday.

"Everything will be all right if the water lowers and the pressure on the dikes eases. It is possible to assume that the dikes will hold although the situation (in Slubice) is still very dangerous," Marek Sobczak, an official of the flood crisis committee, told Reuters.
He said about 2,000 evacuated inhabitants had returned to Slubice at the weekend, but there was still a chance water could seep through the community's sodden dikes.
"If the water does not lower significantly -- 20 to 40 cm (eight to 16 inches) in a 24-hour period -- there will always be a real threat dikes will give," he said.

More than 100 people have died in flooding in Poland and the Czech Republic. In Poland alone, 162,500 people were evacuated, 57 towns were submerged by water and damage has run into billions of dollars.
More than 186,000 hectares (460,000 acres) are still flooded and about 43,800 evacuees remain away from home.
The government plans massive reconstruction of the stricken areas and will consider introducing a special flood tax or tax-deductible bonds in 1998 to help finance rebuilding.
Opposition parties have strongly criticised the ruling coalition of ex-communists (SLD) and peasants (PSL) for the way they handled the crisis.
